observations: Unchanged programs varied between launches; temporary profiling found CPU sections slowing together while GPU drain time fell. The benchmark did not execute the application frame delay.
A hidden macOS process could report interactive main-thread QoS while retaining a background application role. Sleep prevention alone did not fix throughput variation.
The final test uses SDL foreground-on-launch and a scoped NSProcessInfo activity. It makes no production scheduling change and adds no per-frame work.
